description: Crash log in, culprit shortlist out. Parses the log, then correlates its suspects with the loaded plugins and (with a gameId) the known-conflict database into one bundle: which suspected mods are actually in the load order, at what index, and which loaded plugins have known conflicts, plus, kept apart and capped at 10, LOOT's notes on the plugins the log lists (general advice, not evidence about the crash). It lines up the evidence; it does NOT name the cause — that's the model's call, reasoned over the data. Lower-level: when the user asks why their game crashed or which mod it is, use mw_crash_whisperer instead, which reads the log, ranks the suspects and writes the help posts. Use this when the user wants this correlation bundle itself. Opt-in attribution (attributeSuspects=true) links up to 5 suspects to their Nexus mod pages — author, link, and the name it matched, since a name search can mismatch; off by default, so nothing about the suspects leaves the computer. With a gameId the known-conflict check fetches LOOT's public list from GitHub, which sends nothing from the log.

attributeSuspects.description: Opt-in, off by default: resolve up to 5 named suspects to their Nexus mod pages (author + link) so the user can reach the author. Requires gameId and a stored Nexus credential; makes bounded network calls to api.nexusmods.com only when true. Default: no call to Nexus (with a gameId the known-conflict check still fetches LOOT's public list from GitHub).

gameId.description: Canonical game id (e.g. 'skyrimspecialedition', 'fallout4') to include the known-conflict cross-check, and to scope attribution if requested. Omit to skip both.

logContent.description: Crashlog content as a string. Provide this OR logPath.

logPath.description: Absolute path to a crashlog on disk (the SKSE/F4SE crash folder, or the game's BepInEx/LogOutput.log).

logType.description: Format hint. Default 'auto' — detect from content.

name: mw_diagnose_crash
title: Diagnose a crash
